haiku-low.q1: In step 4, after build and lint pass and before the new release starts. The old colour keeps serving and must work on the new schema, since the rule is additive-only.
haiku-low.q2: NOT STATED. The lint rejects drops, renames and type changes in new migration files, but the document does not say when such changes may happen.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 instances must pass /healthz 3 times in a row, and smoke tests must pass, within 10 minutes of starting. If not, the deploy aborts with no user traffic moved.
haiku-low.q4: One operation repoints the public listener from the old target group to the new one, moving all traffic at once with no gradual shift. The pipeline then reads the listener back to confirm.
haiku-low.q5: 5xx rate above 1% over 5 minutes, or the metric unreadable for 3 minutes, during the 15-minute watch. Rollback repoints the listener to the old group, sets rolled_back, alerts, and stops the new colour. Migrations and the old colour are left alone.
haiku-low.q6: Until 30 minutes after switched_at. After that, a problem is handled as a normal deploy of the previous release, going through all steps again.
haiku-low.q7: A failed migration rolls back its own transaction, so it leaves no partial change. A failed concurrent index build leaves an invalid index that is dropped before retry. The deploy stops, the new release never starts, the live colour keeps serving, and step 12 runs.
haiku-low.q8: The live colour is read from the public listener's target group; the other colour is the new one. The deploy record in the deploy_state table stores the colours but never decides which is live.
haiku-low.q9: The CI concurrency group catalog-web-deploy allows only one deploy at a time. The lock is held until step 12, after the old colour shuts down, and CI frees it if the job dies.
haiku-low.q10: A second listener on the same load balancer, on a private port reachable only by CI runners, forwards to the new colour's target group. It carries no user traffic.
haiku-low.q11: The pipeline applies pending migrations once, in step 4; instances never run migrations. The document does not describe any other mechanism that enforces the once-only rule.
haiku-low.q12: Abort and rollback both stop the new colour's instances, leaving it idle. Any instances still running there are stopped by step 2 of the next deploy, so it starts from an idle colour.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after build/lint and before the new release starts (step 5). The old colour (still live) must keep working on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive-only.
sonnet.q2: NOT STATED (the lint rejects drops and renames in a deploy; the document does not say when they are allowed).
sonnet.q3: All 4 instances must be ready (3 consecutive /healthz passes each, checked every 10s) and the smoke suite must pass, all within 10 minutes of instances_started_at. If not, the deploy aborts: the new colour's instances are stopped, the public listener is left alone, status is set to aborted, on-call is alerted, and it goes to step 12.
sonnet.q4: One operation repoints the public listener from the old colour's target group to the new one. All traffic moves at once, with no gradual shift. The pipeline reads the listener back to confirm.
sonnet.q5: Trigger: during the 15-minute watch (step 9), the 5xx rate over the last 5 minutes (or time since switch if shorter) is above 1%, or the 5xx metric is unreadable for 3 minutes. Changes: repoints the listener to the old target group (only if it currently points at the new one), sets status rolled_back and alerts, stops the new colour's instances. Left alone: database migrations (not reversed) and the old colour, which is live again.
sonnet.q6: Until switched_at + 30 minutes (the old colour stays running). After that, a problem is handled by a normal deploy of the previous release through all the steps; its migrations are already applied, so step 4 does nothing.
sonnet.q7: A failed migration rolls back its own transaction. A failed concurrent index build leaves an invalid index, which the migration tool drops before the next attempt. The deploy stops, the new release is never started, and the live colour keeps serving. Status set to failed and on-call alerted; step 12 still runs.
sonnet.q8: Step 2 reads which target group the public listener points at. That colour is the old/live colour and the other is the new one. The live colour is never recorded as authoritative, only read from the listener. The deploy_state row in PostgreSQL records the old and new colour, but it never decides which colour is live.
sonnet.q9: The CI concurrency group lock named catalog-web-deploy. Only the newest waiting deploy runs. It is held from step 1 until step 12, after the old colour has been shut down (or after abort, rollback or failure). A waiting deploy waits up to 60 minutes.
sonnet.q10: Through a test listener: a second listener on the same load balancer, on a private port reachable only by CI runners. It is pointed at the new colour's target group and carries no user traffic.
sonnet.q11: The pipeline (CI) applies pending migrations to the shared database in step 4. Instances never run migrations. The document does not state a further mechanism for once-only execution beyond this: the pipeline runs them once per deploy, and a later deploy of the previous release finds them already applied.
sonnet.q12: Both abort and rollback stop the new colour's instances, so it is left idle. For the next deploy, step 2 also stops any instances still running on the new colour from an earlier failed deploy, so the idle colour starts clean.
